morning: Morning. Bread's still warm if you're quick.
Up with the sun, same as ever.
Fine morning for it, whatever it is you do.
workam: Work won't do itself.
Busy hands, quiet mind.
The day's half spent already, feels like.
midday: Best hour of the day — the eating one.
The square's lively this time of day.
workpm: Long stretch till supper.
Back at it, then.
The afternoon drags, doesn't it?
evening: Day's done. Now for the good part.
You'll find half the town at the square tonight.
Evenings like this, you almost forget the mountain's full of monsters.
night: Quiet streets tonight. Keep them that way, eh?
friendly: Good to see you about!
There you are! The town's better with you in it.
If you ever need a roof, you know where mine is.

workam: Ore's been good this week.
Hear that ring? That's honest work.
Mind the sparks, friend.
workpm: A blade's only as good as the arm that works the bellows.
Bring me ingots and I'll show you what they can be.
This forge hasn't gone cold in twenty years.
evening: Arms like lead. Good day's work.
The forge sleeps, and soon, so do I.
friendly: For you? I'd fire the forge at midnight.
My best work's always waiting for you, friend.

workam: Move along. Politely, mind.
All quiet at the mouth. The way we like it.
You heading down? Come back up, that's an order.
workpm: Keep clear of the dungeon mouth unless you mean it.
Twenty years and the wall's never been breached. Not on my round.
evening: Night shift takes over soon. Poor sods.
Streets clear out fast when the light goes.
night: Late for a walk. Stay under the lamps.
The night round's quiet. Let's keep it so.
If you hear anything from the mountain, you come tell me.
friendly: Sleep easy tonight — I've got the mouth watched.
You've done this town more good than my whole company. Don't repeat that.

workam: Fresh stock, fair prices. Mostly.
Everything's for sale, friend. Everything.
Buy something or stand somewhere else, eh?
workpm: Prices like these won't last. They never do.
The dungeon takes gold down, you bring it back up. I like the arrangement.
evening: Counting the till. Don't stand so close.
Come back tomorrow, the good stock arrives at dawn.
friendly: For my favourite customer? I might shave the price a little.
You bring the coin, I'll keep the best under the counter for you.

morning: The light finds us all, even down in the dark.
workam: The temple's open to anyone the dungeon has chewed on.
Faith mends what bandages can't.
workpm: Come in bleeding, leave whole. That's the arrangement.
The divine doesn't haggle, but I'm told my rates are fair.
evening: Evening prayers soon. You're welcome to stay.
Rest. Even the divine rested.
friendly: The light keeps a special watch on you, I think.
You've been good to this town. It's noticed.

workam: Stance first. Everything else is decoration.
The dungeon doesn't grade on effort.
Every scar out there is a lesson someone skipped in here.
workpm: Magic's just discipline wearing a fancy coat.
Show me your affinity and I'll show you what it's worth.
evening: Training's done. The tavern isn't.
Rest is part of the regimen. The best part.
friendly: You? You I'd put against anything on floor ten.
Best student I've had in years. Don't tell the others.

workam: Bit early, but I don't judge.
The kegs don't tap themselves.
evening: What'll it be? We've got ale, and we've got ale.
Busiest hour of the day, bless it.
Mind the dwarf in the corner, he's had four.
night: Last call was an hour ago, friend.
Off home with you. The ale will keep.
friendly: First one's on the house. Don't spread it around.
Your usual corner's free.

workam: Don't breathe the green one.
Everything's a poison in the right dose. Cheerful thought.
workpm: The mushrooms from the deep floors fetch a fine price, if you're diving.
Careful with that shelf. And that one. All of them, really.
friendly: I've a tonic that might interest you. Friends' rates.
You're one of the few who knocks. I appreciate that.

workam: Good wood's worth more than gold some winters.
Measure twice. The dungeon only lets you cut once.
workpm: Half this town leans on my joinery and doesn't know it.
The forest gives, the saw shapes.
friendly: That door of yours squeaking? I'll see to it, no charge.

workam: The trainer says I can't hold a sword till I'm taller.
Have you REALLY been in the dungeon?
evening: Bet you can't catch me!
Ma says the dungeon-divers are heroes. Are you one?
night: I'm not supposed to be out...
Don't tell Ma I'm out here.
friendly: When I grow up I want to be exactly like you!
I told everyone I know you!

morning: These old bones knew the town when the walls were half-built.
Another sunrise. I count them now.
midday: In my day the divers came back with better manners.
Sit, sit. The soup's better with company.
evening: The mountain's moods change, you know. I've watched them for sixty years.
Mind the dungeon, child. It minds you.
friendly: You remind me of someone I knew. That's a compliment.
Come by more often. The stories don't tell themselves.

workam: Water tower won't mind itself.
Honest work, decent pay, no monsters. I'll take it.
workpm: Nearly done for the day. Nearly.
They say the divers earn more in an hour. They earn it, mind.
friendly: You're all right, you know that?
Any time you want a quieter trade, I'll put a word in.
